external.interface:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.
external.qualification: Actual carrier, retained hypotheses apply; published status is existing evidence, not a new audit.

external.interface:
For a rank-$n$ $\mathbb F$-vector bundle $E\to X$, its **frame bundle**
$\operatorname{Fr}(E)$ has fiber

$$\operatorname{Fr}(E)_x=\{u:\mathbb F^n\xrightarrow{\cong}E_x \text{ linear}\}.$$

Its right action is precomposition, $u\cdot g=u\circ g$. A linear bundle
chart identifies the frames with
$U\times\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F)$ and the action with right
multiplication, so $\operatorname{Fr}(E)$ is a principal bundle as in
[[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]].

Conversely, for a right principal $\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F)$-bundle
$P\to X$, let the group act on $\mathbb F^n$ on the left by its standard
representation. The associated bundle

$$P\times_{\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F)}\mathbb F^n$$

is a locally trivial bundle with fiber $\mathbb F^n$ by
[[prop-associated-bundle-is-locally-trivial-and-functorial-under-pullback]].
On the fiber over $x$, choose $p\in P_x$ and set
$$[p,v]+[p,w]=[p,v+w],\qquad a[p,v]=[p,av].$$
Changing $p$ to $pg$ replaces $v,w$ by $g^{-1}v,g^{-1}w$, so these operations
are well-defined because $g$ is linear. The associated local trivializations
restrict to linear isomorphisms on fibers. Thus this is a rank-$n$ vector
bundle in the sense of [[def-real-and-complex-topological-vector-bundle]].
Evaluation

$$[u,v]\longmapsto u(v)$$

is well-defined because $(u\cdot g)(v)=u(gv)$, and it gives a canonical
isomorphism
$\operatorname{Fr}(E)\times_{\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F)}
\mathbb F^n\cong E$. These constructions commute with pullback.
A linear chart numeration induces the same support-subordinate numeration on
the frame bundle and conversely. For $n=0$ the structure group and every frame
fiber are singletons.

external.interface:
Let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle as in
[[def-smooth-principal-g-bundle]]. A **smooth gauge transformation** of $P$ is
a smooth diffeomorphism $\Phi:P\to P$ satisfying
$$\pi\circ\Phi=\pi,\qquad \Phi(pg)=\Phi(p)g\quad(p\in P,\ g\in G).$$
Here diffeomorphism has the meaning of
[[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]]. The **gauge
group** $\mathcal G(P)$ is the set of these transformations under composition.
The identity is a smooth diffeomorphism and composites of smooth maps are
smooth by
[[prop-identity-maps-and-composites-of-smooth-maps-are-smooth]]; composites of
diffeomorphisms are diffeomorphisms because their inverses are composites of
the smooth inverses. The identity covers $M$ and commutes with the right
action. If $\Phi,\Psi\in\mathcal G(P)$, then $\Phi\circ\Psi$ covers $M$ and
$(\Phi\circ\Psi)(pg)=\Phi(\Psi(p)g)=\Phi(\Psi(p))g$, so the conditions are
closed under composition. The inverse of such a $\Phi$ also covers $M$: if
$q=\Phi(p)$ then $\pi(\Phi^{-1}(q))=\pi(p)=\pi(q)$. Equivariance gives
$$\Phi^{-1}(qg)=\Phi^{-1}(\Phi(p)g)=\Phi^{-1}(\Phi(pg))=pg.$$
Its smoothness is part of the diffeomorphism condition. Hence these maps form a
group under the composition law of [[def-group]].

The structure group $G$ acts on each fibre of $P$, while $\mathcal G(P)$ acts
on the total bundle by automorphisms over the identity map of $M$. They are
different groups: a gauge transformation may vary from fibre to fibre, and
this definition assigns no topology or finite-dimensional Lie-group structure
to $\mathcal G(P)$.

external.interface:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. Tensoriality of $R$ is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a).
Lowering its output slot with the smooth metric and contracting with the
smooth inverse metric are intrinsic tensor operations
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] clauses (b)-(c),
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]]). Thus these formulas give smooth
fields of types $(0,4)$, $(0,2)$, $(0,0)$ and $(0,2)$, respectively,
independent of the chart. Symmetry of $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $G$ is proved
separately in [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clause (d).

external.interface:
This item assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ through the tangent-bundle and
manifold-product suppliers cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]); no further
choice principle is used.

**(a) Data.** Let $c>0$ be a real constant. An **FLRW model datum with
conversion constant $c$** is a tuple

$$(I,\Sigma,\gamma,k,a)$$

consisting of:

1. a nonempty open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$, the **time interval**
   ([[def-interval]]);
2. a spatial model datum $(\Sigma,\gamma,k)$: a connected smooth
   three-manifold $\Sigma$ without boundary, a Riemannian metric $\gamma$ on
   $\Sigma$, and a normalized curvature parameter $k\in\{-1,0,1\}$ with
   $\operatorname{Ric}(\gamma)=2k\gamma$
   ([[def-gr-flrw-spatial-model]], [[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]],
   [[def-smooth-manifold]]);
3. a **scale factor**: a smooth map $a:I\to(0,\infty)$, with values in the open
   interval of strictly positive reals
   ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]).

Its **spacetime** is the product manifold $M:=I\times\Sigma$ with the product
smooth structure
([[prop-products-of-smooth-manifolds-have-a-canonical-product-smooth-structure]]),
a smooth four-manifold without boundary. We write $t:M\to I$ for the first
coordinate function, the **cosmic time**, and $\dot a:=\frac{d}{dt}a$ for the
derivative of the scale factor ([[def-derivative]]).

**(b) The FLRW metric.** In product charts $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ with $x^0=t$,
where $(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ is a smooth chart of $\Sigma$, define the component functions

$$g_{00}:=-c^2,\qquad g_{0i}:=g_{i0}:=0,\qquad g_{ij}:=a(t)^2\gamma_{ij},\qquad i,j\in\{1,2,3\}.$$

These functions are smooth on the chart domain, and they define a smooth
symmetric covariant two-tensor field $g$ on $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]): the component transformation
law is that of a symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor because the definitions agree on
chart overlaps, the time component is constant and the spatial components are
multiplied by the common smooth factor $a(t)^2$. The field $g$ is the
**FLRW metric** of the datum; we write the standard informal display
$g=-c^2\,dt^2+a(t)^2\,\gamma$, meaning the symmetric tensor $-c^2\,dt\otimes dt+a(t)^2\gamma$.
That $g$ is a Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ and that the coordinate field $\partial_t$ is a time
orientation for it are not asserted by this definition but proved in
[[lem-gr-flrw-metric-and-comoving-data]] on this page; the same holds for the
clauses below that use the metric's causal classification.

**(c) Comoving congruence and cosmic time direction.** The **comoving
congruence** of the datum is the smooth vector field
$n:=c^{-1}\partial_t$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). By
[[lem-gr-flrw-metric-and-comoving-data]] the field $n$ is a smooth
future-directed unit timelike field, $g(n,n)=-1$, and the **comoving
observers** of the datum are its maximal integral curves; in product
coordinates the integral curve through $(t_0,x)$ is
$s\mapsto(t_0+s/c,x)$ on $c(I-t_0)$. Its proper-time parametrization is the
**comoving curve** $t\mapsto(t,x)$ on $I$, with constant spatial coordinate
$x\in\Sigma$ and velocity $U=cn=\partial_t$.

**(d) Hubble parameter and expansion.** The **Hubble parameter** of the datum
is the smooth function

$$H:=\frac{\dot a}{a}:I\to\mathbb R .$$

No field equation, no matter content, no equation of state, no measured value
and no claim about nature is part of this definition: an FLRW model datum is a
geometric object, and the physical reading of $c$, of $t$ as a clock reading,
of $n$ as the matter rest congruence and of $H$ as an expansion rate is
recorded in the physical postulates of the framework, not here.
external.qualification: Actual carrier, retained hypotheses apply; published status is existing evidence, not a new audit.

external.interface:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\xi$ be a smooth vector field
on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **Lie
derivative of the metric along $\xi$**, written $\mathcal L_\xi g$, is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field obtained by the flow definition of
[[def-lie-derivative-of-a-tensor-field]] applied to $g$: for the local flow
$\Phi_t$ of $\xi$,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g:=\frac{d}{dt}\Big|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*g .$$

The field $\xi$ is a **Killing field** of $(M,g)$ (an **isometry generator**,
or a **Killing vector**) when

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0 .$$

The equivalent local characterization

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0,$$

where $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and
$\xi_b:=g_{bc}\xi^c$ is the lowered field, is proved in
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]] clause (a); the definition
itself asserts neither direction. Whether a given metric has Killing fields is
a property of that metric: neither existence nor uniqueness of a Killing field
is asserted here, and a general metric has none beyond the trivial field
$\xi=0$.
external.qualification: Actual carrier, retained hypotheses apply; published status is existing evidence, not a new audit.

external.interface:
Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary, so that $M$ is Hausdorff
and second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $g$ be a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]. Then $g$ assigns
to every $p\in M$ a bilinear form $g_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(a) Lorentzian metric.** The field $g$ is a **Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$** on $M$ when it is symmetric and nondegenerate, and at every
$p\in M$ the pair $(T_pM,g_p)$ is a Lorentz vector space of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]: that is, $g_p$ has
inertia $(3,1,0)$, so that some — equivalently every — basis of $T_pM$ in which
the matrix of $g_p$ is diagonal has exactly one negative and three positive
diagonal entries. The pair $(M,g)$ is a **smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** (or
Lorentzian manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$). In a smooth chart $(U,x)$ the
**components** of $g$ are the $C^\infty$ functions
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and $g_{ab}=g_{ba}$ by symmetry.
We use indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ and the Einstein summation convention, with
components in a chart written as lower-case indexed symbols and equations
between indexed fields understood basis-independently. These conventions are
fixed once for this library and the physical reading of the symbols is recorded
with the framework postulates, separately from this mathematical definition.

**(b) Pointwise causal structure.** For every $p\in M$ the vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] applies to the Lorentz vector
space $(T_pM,g_p)$: a tangent vector $v\in T_pM$ is **timelike** when
$g_p(v,v)<0$, **null** when $v\neq0$ and $g_p(v,v)=0$, **spacelike** when
$g_p(v,v)>0$, and **causal** when it is timelike or null. Every nonzero
$v\in T_pM$ has exactly one causal character. The **timelike set**
$T_p:=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\}$ has exactly two connected components, each
nonempty, open, convex and path-connected; each $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ of $T_pM$ satisfies $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
for some ordering, so in particular nonzero orthonormal vectors exist at every
point ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]],
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).

**(c) Time orientation.** A **time orientation** of $(M,g)$, also called a
**choice of future cone**, is a smooth vector field $N$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]], whose tangent-bundle
smooth structure uses the axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of
[[def-countable-choice]]; this is the only use of that axiom in this
definition) such that

$$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in M .$$

The function $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N_p)$ is $C^\infty$ because $g$ is a smooth
covariant $2$-tensor field and $N$ a smooth field, so the condition is a
pointwise strict inequality between a smooth function and $0$; since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0$ implies $N_p\neq0$, a time orientation is nowhere vanishing.
A **time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** is a triple $(M,g,N)$
consisting of a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and a time orientation $N$.

Given a time orientation $N$ and $p\in M$, the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and we
**define** a nonzero causal vector $v\in T_pM$ to be **future-directed** when
$g_p(v,N_p)<0$ and **past-directed** when $g_p(v,N_p)>0$. The classification of
nonzero causal vectors into exactly these two classes, and its agreement with
the two components of the timelike set (the future component is the component
$C_p^+$ containing $N_p$, and the future causal vectors form
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$), is proved in
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]; in particular no
nonzero causal $v$ satisfies $g_p(v,N_p)=0$, so the definition is exhaustive and
mutually exclusive. Replacing $N$ by $-N$ reverses every future/past label, and
two time orientations $N,N'$ determine the same future-directed causal vectors
at every point where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)<0$, while they determine opposite ones
where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)>0$, by
[[lem-gr-timelike-fields-define-equal-or-opposite-future-cones]]; that lemma
also shows the sign of $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N'_p)$ is constant on every connected
component of $M$.

**(d) The inverse metric.** Because $g_p$ is nondegenerate, it induces at each
$p$ an isomorphism $\flat_p:T_pM\to T_p^*M$, $v\mapsto g_p(v,\cdot)$, and an
inverse metric $g_p^{-1}$ on the dual space; the inverse metric, the musical
isomorphisms and the components $g^{ab}$ are defined separately on this page,
where the smoothness of those components is also proved. Neither construction
uses any choice principle beyond the one already recorded in (c).


**(e) Smooth timelike curves and their scalar normalization.** Before using
these quantities in the physical conventions, fix a positive real scaling
parameter $c$ (with no physical meaning or dimension in this mathematical
item). A **smooth future timelike curve** is a smooth map $\gamma:I\to M$
from a nonempty open real interval $I$ ([[def-interval]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) whose velocity derivation
$\gamma'(s)\in T_{\gamma(s)}M$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]]) satisfies
$g(\gamma',\gamma')<0$ and $g(\gamma',N)<0$ at every $s\in I$.
In a chart its components are $d(x^a\circ\gamma)/ds$, $a=0,1,2,3$.
For a supplied base point $s_0\in I$ and additive constant $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$
define

$$h(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s))},\qquad \tau(s):=\tau_0+\frac1c\int_{s_0}^{s}h(r)\,dr,\qquad U(s):=\frac{c\gamma'(s)}{h(s)}.$$

The integral is oriented when $s<s_0$. The function $\tau$ is called
**proper time** for this scaling and $U$ the **four-velocity** of the smooth
curve; its increment times $c$ is the Lorentzian length. The well-definedness
proof below shows $\tau'>0$, that $\tau:I\to\tau(I)$ is a smooth
diffeomorphism, and that $U$ is the velocity of $\gamma\circ\tau^{-1}$.
Thus $g(U,U)=-c^2$ and $U$ is future timelike. This introduces the smooth
case before any physical unit reading; the later worldline definition extends
it to its stated $C^k$, endpoint and piecewise-$C^1$ classes. It asserts no
clock coupling, motion law or physical value of $c$.

**Convention and scope.** The physical reading of a smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold as a classical spacetime model, and the domain in which
that reading is adopted, are recorded in the framework postulate
`post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain`; the words spacetime and event carry no
mathematical content beyond this definition, and this item asserts no claim
about nature. The dimension $4$ and the absence of boundary are part of the
data; nothing in the definition assumes that $M$ is nonempty or connected, and
no completeness, extendibility or maximality property of $(M,g)$ is asserted.
external.qualification: Actual carrier, retained hypotheses apply; published status is existing evidence, not a new audit.

external.interface:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and Einstein tensor $G$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]), let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface
([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]],
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (a)), and fix real
constants $\kappa$ and $\Lambda$ (the framework coupling constants, purely
parameters for this definition).

**(a) The geometric data.**
For $p\in\Sigma$ the orthogonal complement $T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is
one-dimensional and nondegenerate
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]],
[[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]]); there is therefore a unique
$n_p\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ with $g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and $g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$ and it
depends smoothly on $p$, the **future unit normal field** of $\Sigma$; this
and the properties of $h$ and $K$ below are proved, not assumed, in
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]. Define
on $\Sigma$ the **induced metric** $h$ and the **second fundamental form**
$K$ by
$$h_p(V,W):=g_p(V,W),\qquad K_p(V,W):=g_p(\nabla_Vn,W)\qquad(V,W\in T_p\Sigma),$$
where $\nabla_Vn$ is the covariant derivative at $p$ of the ambient field $n$
in the tangential direction $V$; $h$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on
$\Sigma$ and $K$ a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]).

**(b) Matter data and constraints.** Let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on $M$ (the stress-energy field of a matter branch). Its
**matter data on $\Sigma$** are the smooth fields
$$\rho:=T(n,n),\qquad j(V):=-T(n,V)\quad(V\in T\Sigma).$$
The tuple $(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$ **satisfies the constraint equations** for
$(\kappa,\Lambda)$ when
$$G(n,n)-\Lambda=\kappa\,\rho,\qquad G(n,V)=\kappa\,T(n,V)\quad\text{for every }V\in T_p\Sigma,\ p\in\Sigma .$$
The first is the normal projection of the equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$
evaluated on $(n,n)$, namely $G(n,n)+\Lambda g(n,n)=\kappa T(n,n)$, with
$g(n,n)=-1$; the second is the normal-tangential projection, the term in
$\Lambda$ dropping because $g(n,V)=0$. That a solution of the field equation
satisfies these two projections is proved in
[[lem-gr-constraint-projections]]. The purely tangential projection
$G(V,W)+\Lambda h(V,W)=\kappa T(V,W)$ is not part of the constraints and is
not required here.

**(c) Developments.** A **development** of the data
$(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
$(M',g',N')$ together with a smooth embedding $\varphi:\Sigma\to M'$ whose
image is a spacelike embedded hypersurface with induced metric $\varphi^*g'=h$
and second fundamental form $K$ with respect to its future unit normal $n'$.
Write $T'$ for the smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field included as
the development's stress-energy field. Require the tensor equation
$$G'+\Lambda g'=\kappa T'$$
at every point of $M'$, where $G'$ is the Einstein tensor of $g'$ with its
metric-selected connection, defined as above. The constants $\kappa$ and
$\Lambda$ are the fixed parameters of the initial data. The matter-data matching condition is
the pair of normal projections
$$\rho(p)=T'_{\varphi(p)}(n'_{\varphi(p)},n'_{\varphi(p)}),\qquad j_p(V)=-T'_{\varphi(p)}(n'_{\varphi(p)},d\varphi_p(V))\quad(p\in\Sigma,\ V\in T_p\Sigma).$$
Equivalently, the scalar field $T'(n',n')$ along $\varphi(\Sigma)$ pulls
back to $\rho$, and the covector field $-T'(n',\cdot)$ restricted to
$T\varphi(\Sigma)$ pulls back to $j$. This tuple prescribes only these
stress-energy projections; any additional matter-field data are not included
in $(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$. The development is a **globally hyperbolic
development** when
$\varphi(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy hypersurface of $(M',g',N')$. The implication
from this Cauchy property to global hyperbolicity of $(M',g',N')$ is a
separate theorem, deferred to the later causal theory; it is not established
by this definition
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]],
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c)).

**(d) Maximality.** A globally hyperbolic development $(M_*,g_*,N_*;
\varphi_*)$ is **maximal** for the data when for every globally hyperbolic
development $(M',g',N';\varphi')$ there is a smooth isometric embedding
$\psi:M'\to M_*$ with $\psi\circ\varphi'=\varphi_*$, $\psi$ preserving the
time orientations and carrying the selected stress-energy tensor $T'$ to
$T_*$, that is, $\psi^*T_*=T'$. This is a universal embedding property: every globally hyperbolic
development embeds into the selected maximal one with its data and
stress-energy tensor preserved. It does not assert that arbitrary globally
hyperbolic developments are mutually isometric.

**(e) Scope.** The definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of
developments, and it does not assert that $T'$ is generated by matter fields
solving any equation: those claims require the local and global existence theory of
the Einstein-matter system and are not made on this page. The constraint
equations are displayed only as equations satisfied or not by given data.
The equivalent formulation of the constraints in terms of the induced scalar

solutions of the constraints, rest on the Gauss-Codazzi relations and on PDE
theory and are deferred to the later pages of this track; no such
equivalence is asserted here.

Let $(M,g,N)=(\mathbb R^4,\eta,\partial_0)$ be the flat model with its
inertial chart $x$ and metric components
$\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$
([[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Since the chart identifies each
$T_p\mathbb R^4$ with $\mathbb R^4$, all objects below are defined by their
components in this chart; they are the components at a point, and a subscript
$p$ is suppressed. Indices are raised and lowered with $\eta$ and $\eta^{-1}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]), and orthogonality is in
the sense of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]].

**(a) Observer, propagation direction, screen.** Let $n=n^a\partial_a$ be an
**observer** of the flat model: $n$ is future-directed, $\eta(n,n)=-1$
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]); and let
$s=s^a\partial_a$ be a **propagation direction**: $\eta(s,s)=1$ and
$\eta(n,s)=0$. The pair defines the two-dimensional **screen**
$\Sigma(n,s):=\{v\in\mathbb R^4:\eta(v,n)=0,\ \eta(v,s)=0\}$, on which the
restriction of $\eta$ is positive definite by
[[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]. The **screen projector** and
the **spatial projector** of the pair are the $(1,1)$-tensors with components

$$p^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b-s^as_b,\qquad h^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b,$$

and the covariant form of the screen projector is
$p_{ab}:=\eta_{ac}p^c{}_b=\eta_{ab}+n_an_b-s_as_b$. The properties $p^2=p$,
$h^2=h$, $\operatorname{im}p=\Sigma(n,s)$ and $\operatorname{im}h=n^\perp$
are proved in the screen-projector lemma of this page.

**(b) TT projection.** Let $A=(A_{ab})$ be a symmetric covariant $2$-tensor
at a point. Its **transverse-traceless (TT) projection with respect to
$(n,s)$** is the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor

$$\Pi_{n,s}(A)_{ab}:=p_a{}^cp_b{}^dA_{cd}-\tfrac12\,p_{ab}\,p^{cd}A_{cd},\qquad p^{cd}:=\eta^{ce}\eta^{df}p_{ef}.$$

**(c) Screen amplitudes.** Let $(e_1,e_2)$ be an ordered
$\eta$-orthonormal basis of $\Sigma(n,s)$ (which exists by
[[cor-finite-dimensional-inner-product-spaces-have-orthonormal-bases]] applied
to the positive-definite restriction of $\eta$). For a symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor $A$ the **plus and cross amplitudes of $A$ with respect to
$(e_1,e_2)$** are $A_+:=A(e_1,e_1)$ and $A_\times:=A(e_1,e_2)$; if $A$ is
TT with respect to $(n,s)$ in the sense of clause (d) below, then, extending
the screen dual basis to covectors on $\mathbb R^4$ by
$e^i(v):=\eta(e_i,v)$ for $i=1,2$ (so both vanish on $n,s$),

$$A=A_+\bigl(e^1\otimes e^1-e^2\otimes e^2\bigr)+A_\times\bigl(e^1\otimes e^2+e^2\otimes e^1\bigr).$$

For a TT screen tensor $A$, under the rotation
$e_1'=\cos\theta\,e_1+\sin\theta\,e_2$,
$e_2'=-\sin\theta\,e_1+\cos\theta\,e_2$ of the screen basis the amplitudes
transform as $A_+'=A_+\cos2\theta+A_\times\sin2\theta$ and
$A_\times'=-A_+\sin2\theta+A_\times\cos2\theta$. Here $\sin$ and $\cos$
are the power-series functions of [[def-sine-and-cosine-by-power-series]];
expanding $A(e_1',e_1')$ and $A(e_1',e_2')$ by bilinearity and applying the
addition formulas of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas]] gives the two
displayed transformations.

**(d) TT tensors and TT perturbations.** A symmetric covariant $2$-tensor
$A$ is **transverse-traceless (TT) with respect to $(n,s)$** when
$A(n,\cdot)=0$, $A(s,\cdot)=0$ and $\eta^{ab}A_{ab}=0$. For a symmetric
field $h$ on a nonempty open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^4$, use the
constant smooth extensions of the fixed component vectors:
$n_q:=n^a\partial_a|_q$ and $s_q:=s^a\partial_a|_q$ for $q\in\Omega$.
Here a symmetric field is a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field with symmetric
components in the sense of [[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]. Then
"TT with respect to $(n,s)$" means
$h_q(n_q,\cdot)=h_q(s_q,\cdot)=0$ and $\eta^{ab}h_{ab}(q)=0$ for every
$q\in\Omega$. It is **spatial with respect to $n$** when
$h_q(n_q,\cdot)=0$ for every $q\in\Omega$.

**(e) Scope.** This item fixes the screen, the two projections and the
amplitude terminology, and states the rotation law of clause (c) as part of
the naming. It asserts no property of $\Pi_{n,s}$ (idempotence, rank, image
and trace are proved in the screen-projector lemma of this page), no relation
to the planar perturbations of the plane-wave definition of this page
(established in the gauge-decomposition lemma of this page) and no physical
interpretation of the amplitudes.

a smooth manifold. A **smooth right principal $G$-bundle** is a right principal
$G$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$ in the topological sense of
[[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]], with the following
additional smooth structure: $\pi$ and the right $G$-action are smooth, and
the principal-bundle charts can be chosen as equivariant diffeomorphisms
$\pi^{-1}(U)\cong U\times G$. Thus each chart respects the projection to
$U$ and the right action on the $G$ factor. The smoothness convention is that
of [[def-smooth-map-between-manifolds-with-boundary]]; boundaryless manifolds
are the default in this item.

action on every fibre and its local triviality. Smoothness adds compatible
differentiable structure; it does not select a connection or assert that a
global trivialization exists. The empty-base case is allowed and then $P$ is
empty by the cited topological definition.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) for the absolutely continuous causal-curve
calculus and the supplied causal results used below.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$F\subseteq M$ be an open future set, so that $I^+(F)=F$
([[def-gr-future-and-past-sets]] clause (a)), and let $A:=\partial F$ be its
achronal boundary. Then:

**(a) Achronality.** $A$ is closed and achronal: no two distinct points of
$A$ are chronologically related in either direction. Consequently every
future or past timelike curve meets $A$ in at most one point.

**(b) Local Lipschitz graph.** For every $p\in A$ there are a chart
$(U,x)$ of the kind produced by [[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a)
and (d) around $p$, with $x(p)=0$, domination constant $K$, and minorant
coefficient $c=16$, and numbers
$a,\rho>0$ with $W:=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times B_\rho(0)\bigr)\subseteq U$, such
that for every $z\in B_\rho(0)$ the coordinate vertical line
$$L_z:=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times\{z\}\bigr)$$
meets $A\cap W$ in exactly one point, and there is a function
$\varphi:B_\rho(0)\to(-a,a)$ with
$$A\cap W=\bigl\{x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z):z\in B_\rho(0)\bigr\},\qquad |\varphi(z)-\varphi(z')|\le\sqrt c\,|z-z'|\quad (z,z'\in B_\rho(0)).$$
Thus $A$ is locally the graph of a Lipschitz function of the spatial
coordinates of the chart.

**(c) Topological hypersurface.** The maps $z\mapsto x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$ of
(b), for all points $p\in A$, form a topological atlas on $A$: $A$ is a
topological $3$-manifold in the subspace topology and its inclusion into $M$
is a topological embedding. No smoothness of $A$ is asserted.

**(d) Null measure.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mu$ be a measure on the Borel sets of $M$
which is locally absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure:
whenever $(V,y)$ is a chart and $E\subseteq V$ has $y(E)$ of four-dimensional
Lebesgue measure zero, then $\mu(E)=0$. Then $\mu(A\cap K)=0$ for every
compact $K\subseteq M$. In particular this holds for every smooth positive
volume density on $M$.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) for the absolutely continuous causal-curve

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ and the relations $\ll$, $\le$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** if $p\ll q$ and $q\le r$, then $p\ll r$;

**(b)** if $p\le q$ and $q\ll r$, then $p\ll r$;

**(c)** if $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ is a future causal curve and there are
$a\le s<t\le b$ such that $\gamma|_{[s,t]}$ is a future timelike curve, then
$\gamma(a)\ll\gamma(b)$;

**(d)** consequently
$$I^+\bigl(J^+(\Omega)\bigr)=I^+(\Omega),\qquad I^-\bigl(J^-(\Omega)\bigr)=I^-(\Omega)$$
for every $\Omega\subseteq M$, and dually
$J^+\bigl(I^+(\Omega)\bigr)=I^+(\Omega)$.

No choice principle beyond the stated assumptions is used.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
globally hyperbolic time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)), let
$L_g$ be the Lebesgue Lorentzian length functional on locally absolutely continuous future causal curves
([[lem-gr-normal-neighborhood-length-monotonicity]], with nonzero future causal velocity almost everywhere), and for $q\in M$ define the
**time separation**
$$\tau_q:M\to[0,\infty),\qquad \tau_q(r):=\sup\{L_g(\alpha):\ \alpha \text{ is a future causal curve from } r \text{ to } q\},$$
the supremum over the empty set being $0$; thus $\tau_q(r)>0$ exactly for
$r\in I^-(q)$ and $\tau_q(r)=0$ for $r\notin J^-(q)$.

**(a)** For every $r\in J^-(q)$ one has $0\le\tau_q(r)<\infty$. If $r\ne q$, the supremum is attained by a future causal curve $\gamma$ from $r$ to $q$ with $L_g(\gamma)=\tau_q(r)$. Every such **nondegenerate maximizer** is, up to increasing reparametrization, a causal geodesic, with image in the compact set $J^+(r)\cap J^-(q)$. For $r=q$, $\tau_q(q)=0$ and the constant zero-velocity geodesic is the **degenerate maximizer** by convention. It has image $\{q\}$ and length zero; it is not asserted to belong to the curve class requiring nonzero causal velocity almost everywhere. This separates the reflexive case without changing the separation function or the nondegenerate maximizing claim.

**(b)** Let $V$ be a strictly convex normal neighbourhood of $q$ (as produced
by [[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) and let $W\subseteq V$ be open and
causally convex in $M$ (every causal curve in $M$ with both endpoints in $W$
is contained in $W$), with $\overline W$ compact and $q\in W$. Then for every
$r\in W\cap I^-(q)$,
$$\tau_q(r)=\sqrt{-g_q\bigl(\exp_q^{-1}(r),\exp_q^{-1}(r)\bigr)},$$
so $\tau_q$ is smooth on $W\cap I^-(q)$ and extends continuously by
$\tau_q(q)=0$ and $\tau_q(r)=0$ for $r\in W\setminus J^-(q)$.

**(c)** On every compact set $K\subseteq M$ the function $\tau_q$ is upper
semicontinuous in the following strong form: for every sequence $r_n\to r$ in
$K$ one has $\limsup_n\tau_q(r_n)\le\tau_q(r)$. If moreover $r\in I^-(q)$,
then $\tau_q(r_n)\to\tau_q(r)$ for every sequence $r_n\to r$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $K$ be a compact
Hausdorff group with normalized Haar probability measure $\mu$
([[cor-normalized-haar-probability-on-a-compact-group]]), and let
$\pi:K\to U(H)$ and $\sigma:K\to U(J)$ be strongly continuous unitary
representations of $K$ on complex Hilbert spaces $H$ and $J$
([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]], [[def-hilbert-space]]).
Write
$$\operatorname{Hom}_K(H,J):=\{T\in\mathcal B(H,J):T\pi(g)=\sigma(g)T\text{ for every }g\in K\}$$
for the space of bounded intertwiners and let
$A:\mathcal B(H,J)\to\mathcal B(H,J)$ be the Haar averaging operator of
[[def-haar-averaging-operator-on-hom-spaces]], so that
$$\langle A(T)v,w\rangle=\int_K\langle\sigma(k)T\pi(k)^{-1}v,w\rangle\,d\mu(k)$$
for all $T\in\mathcal B(H,J)$, $v\in H$, $w\in J$. Then:

1. $A$ is idempotent, $A\circ A=A$, and its range is exactly
   $\operatorname{Hom}_K(H,J)$: $A(T)$ intertwines for every bounded $T$, and
   $A(T)=T$ for every bounded intertwiner $T$;
2. $A$ is a contraction, $\|A(T)\|\le\|T\|$ for every $T\in\mathcal B(H,J)$,
   hence $\|A\|\le1$;
3. $\|A\|=1$ if $\operatorname{Hom}_K(H,J)\ne\{0\}$, and $\|A\|=0$ if
   $\operatorname{Hom}_K(H,J)=\{0\}$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal $n$, induced Riemannian metric $h$ and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, $R^h$ for its curvature operator in the same operator convention as the ambient curvature, and $S_h$ for its scalar curvature. Explicitly distinguish the lowered tensor from the operator pairing by setting
$$\mathcal R^g(A,B,C,D):=g(R^g(C,D)B,A),\qquad \mathcal R^h(A,B,C,D):=h(R^h(C,D)B,A).$$
Thus $\mathcal R^g_{abcd}=R_{abcd}$ in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=\mathcal R^g(W,Z,X,Y)$. Let $G$ be the Einstein tensor defined there. At every $p\in\Sigma$ and for all $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$\mathcal R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=\mathcal R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z).$$
Equivalently, in operator order,
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=h(R^h(X,Y)Z,W)+K(Y,Z)K(X,W)-K(X,Z)K(Y,W).$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=(D_YK)(X,Z)-(D_XK)(Y,Z).$$

**(c) Normal projections.** Define $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)=h^{ij}(D_{e_i}K)(e_j,Y)$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$. Then
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12(S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau.$$

**(d) Constraint equations.** If the tensor equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$, for a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $T$ and real constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=\kappa T(n,Y).$$
With $\rho=T(n,n)$ and $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$, the second equation is $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=-\kappa j(Y)$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]) and geodesics as in
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Let $p\in M$ and let
$O\subseteq M$ be an open neighborhood of $p$. Then there are a chart
$(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$ and a radius $r>0$ such that
$C:=x^{-1}(B_r)$, $B_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<r\}$ based at
$0=x(p)$, is contained in $O$ and has the following properties.

**(a) Normal neighborhood of each point.** For every $q\in C$ define
$$W_q:=\bigl\{u\in\mathcal E_q:\ \exp_q(tu)\in C\ \text{for every }t\in[0,1]\bigr\},$$
where $\mathcal E_q$ is the exponential domain of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (d). Then $W_q$ is an
open star-shaped neighborhood of $0$ in $T_qM$, and
$\exp_q|_{W_q}:W_q\to C$ is a diffeomorphism onto $C$.

**(b) Unique contained joining segment.** For all $q,q'\in C$ there is
exactly one geodesic segment joining $q$ to $q'$ whose image is contained in
$C$, namely
$$x_{q,q'}:[0,1]\to C,\qquad x_{q,q'}(t)=\exp_q\bigl(t\,v(q,q')\bigr),$$
where $v(q,q')$ is the two-point inverse velocity of
[[lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism]] clause (c). For $q\ne q'$ the
points $x_{q,q'}(t)$, $0<t<1$, lie in $C$ strictly inside the coordinate
ball, i.e. $|x(x_{q,q'}(t))|_{\mathrm e}<r$; and $x_{q',q}$ is the time
reverse of $x_{q,q'}$ up to affine reparametrization.

**(c) Strict convexity.** In the terminology of
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (b), $C$ is a
strictly convex normal neighborhood; in particular the position vector
$P(q,q')=d(\exp_q)_{v(q,q')}\bigl(v(q,q')\bigr)$ and the squared
displacement $D^2(q,q')=g_q\bigl(v(q,q'),v(q,q')\bigr)$ are defined for all
$q,q'\in C$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with an
orientation, metric-selected connection $\nabla$, metric volume form
$\mathrm{vol}_g$ and current flux $\Phi_J$ as in
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]], and let $J$ be a smooth vector
field on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). Write
$\nabla_aJ^a$ for the divergence of $J$.

**(a) Exterior derivative of the current form.** As smooth $4$-forms on $M$,

$$d\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)=\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

**(b) Flux balance (Stokes).** For every finite smooth singular $4$-chain $C$
of $M$ — a finite formal real sum of smooth singular $4$-simplices, the
library convention `def-smooth-singular-chain-and-cochain-complexes` restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — and the flux
$\Phi_J$ of the induced boundary $3$-chain
([[def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex]],
[[thm-stokes-theorem-for-smooth-singular-chains]]),

$$\Phi_J(\partial C)=\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

Consequently, if $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$ for smooth singular $3$-chains
$\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,B$, then

$$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)+\int_C\bigl(\nabla_aJ^a\bigr)\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

In particular, if $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ on $C$ then
$\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)-\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_J(B)$, and if moreover
$\Phi_J(B)=0$ then $\Phi_J(\Sigma_2)=\Phi_J(\Sigma_1)$: equal charges need a
vanishing side flux, not merely a divergence-free current.

**(c) Non-null face formula.** Let $\sigma$ be a smooth singular $3$-simplex —
a map $\sigma:\Delta^3\to M$ admitting a smooth extension to a neighbourhood
of the standard $3$-simplex inside its affine plane, the convention restated
in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) — that is
non-null at a parameter point $t$
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (c)), with
$v_i:=\sigma_*\partial_i|_t$ spanning the hyperplane $H$ and with the unit
normal $\nu^{*}$ adapted to the ordered basis $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ as in
[[lem-gr-metric-volume-form-patching-and-face-normal]] clause (c); write
$\varepsilon:=g_{\sigma(t)}(\nu^{*},\nu^{*})\in\{-1,1\}$. Then

$$\sigma^{*}\bigl(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g\bigr)(\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)\big|_{t} =\varepsilon\,g_{\sigma(t)}\bigl(J,\nu^{*}\bigr)\sqrt{\bigl|\det\bigl(g_{\sigma(t)}(v_i,v_j)\bigr)\bigr|} .$$

Equivalently, the tangent vector $J$ is decomposed as
$J=\varepsilon g(J,\nu^{*})\nu^{*}+w'$ with $w'\in H$, and only the normal
component contributes to the flux through the face.

external.interface:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $R$ be its
curvature ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]), let
$I,J_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ be intervals with nonempty interior
([[def-interval]]), and let $F:J_0\times I\to M$ be a smooth map. Write
$T:=\partial_tF$ and $J^F:=\partial_rF$; a field along $F$ means a smooth
section of $F^*TM$ over $J_0\times I$, and $D_r,D_t$ are the covariant
derivatives in the two parameters
([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Curvature as the commutator of the two derivatives.** For every smooth
field $V$ along $F$,
$$\bigl(D_tD_r-D_rD_t\bigr)V=R(T,J^F)V .$$

**(b) Geodesic deviation.** Suppose in addition that for every $r\in J_0$ the
curve $t\mapsto F(r,t)$ is a geodesic with affine parameter $t$, that is
$D_tT=0$. Then $D_tJ^F=D_rT$ and
$$D_t^2J^F=R(T,J^F)T .$$
Consequently, for every $r$ the field $t\mapsto J^F(r,t)$ is a Jacobi field
along the geodesic $t\mapsto F(r,t)$
([[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause (b)), and for a geodesic
variation the variation field is a Jacobi field.

**(c) Initial data.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a smooth geodesic and let
$s_0\in I$. For every pair $J_0,J_1\in T_{\gamma(s_0)}M$ there exists exactly
one smooth Jacobi field $J$ along $\gamma$ with
$$J(s_0)=J_0,\qquad D_sJ(s_0)=J_1 .$$
The set of all Jacobi fields along $\gamma$ is a real vector space of
dimension $8$, and $J\mapsto\bigl(J(s_0),D_sJ(s_0)\bigr)$ is a linear
isomorphism onto $T_{\gamma(s_0)}M\oplus T_{\gamma(s_0)}M$.

**(d) The tangential component.** Let $\gamma$ be a smooth geodesic and $J$ a
smooth Jacobi field along it. Then $s\mapsto g(J,\gamma')(s)$ is affine, and

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a

([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)), and let

there exist a smooth function $T:M\to\mathbb R$ and, with $\nabla T$ the
gradient of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]], the
following hold.

**(a)** $T$ is a temporal function in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (e): smooth,
$g(\nabla T,\nabla T)<0$ and $g(\nabla T,N)>0$ everywhere.

**(b)** Every level set $S_c:=T^{-1}(c)$, $c\in\mathbb R$, is a Cauchy
hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clauses (a)
and (c)): it is a spacelike embedded hypersurface and every inextendible
causal curve meets it in exactly one parameter value. In particular $T$ is
surjective.

**(c)** Along every inextendible future-directed causal curve
$T\to+\infty$, and along every inextendible past-directed causal curve
$T\to-\infty$.

**(d)** The vector field $X:=\nabla T/g(\nabla T,\nabla T)$ is smooth,
future-directed timelike, satisfies $X(T)=1$, and is complete
([[def-complete-vector-field]]): every maximal integral curve of $X$ is
defined on all of $\mathbb R$, so by
[[prop-a-vector-field-is-complete-if-and-only-if-its-flow-is-global]] its
flow $\Phi:\mathbb R\times M\to M$ is a global smooth flow
([[def-local-and-global-flow]]).

**(e)** The map $\Psi:\mathbb R\times S_0\to M$, $\Psi(s,z):=\Phi(s,z)$, is
a diffeomorphism and $T(\Psi(s,z))=s$ for all $(s,z)$; equivalently $M$ is
foliated by the Cauchy hypersurfaces $S_c$, each flow line meeting each level
exactly once.

**(f)** Put $\beta:=-1/g(\nabla T,\nabla T)$, a smooth positive function, and
$h_T:=g+\beta\,dT\otimes dT$. Then $g=-\beta\,dT\otimes dT+h_T$;
$h_T(X,\cdot)=0$; and $h_T$ restricted to $\ker dT$ is a smooth Riemannian
metric, so the decomposition $T_pM=\mathbb RX_p\oplus\ker dT_p$ is
$g$-orthogonal with $g(X,X)=-\beta$. Consequently the pullback of $g$ by the
diffeomorphism $\Psi$ has no mixed terms,
$$\Psi^*g=-(\beta\circ\Psi)\,ds^2+h,\qquad h_{(s,z)}(v,w):=g_{\Phi(s,z)}\bigl((d\Phi_s)_zv,(d\Phi_s)_zw\bigr),$$
a sum of a negative definite one-dimensional form and the smooth family of
Riemannian metrics induced on the levels.

Local real branches require nonnegative radicands, and smooth branch formulas away from turning points use strictly positive radicands.
planned.proof_route: Set Sigma g^tt=-(r^2+a^2)^2/Delta+a^2 sin(theta)^2, Sigma g^tphi=-a((r^2+a^2)/Delta-1), Sigma g^phiphi=1/sin(theta)^2-a^2/Delta. After inserting partial_t S=-E and partial_phi S=L, the equation is Delta(S_r prime)^2-[E(r^2+a^2)-aL]^2/Delta+mu^2 r^2+(S_theta prime)^2+(L/sin(theta)-aE sin(theta))^2+mu^2 a^2 cos(theta)^2=0. Group the last angular expression to the constant Q+(L-aE)^2 and rearrange; integrate the specified one-variable square roots on intervals where they are real. This proves local separation without a general integrability claim through turning points.

planned.interface: For a real smooth scalar psi on a fixed Lorentzian background define Q_ab=partial_a psi partial_b psi-(1/2)g_ab g^cd partial_c psi partial_d psi and J_a^X=Q_ab X^b. The test equation is box_g psi=0; the background is not evolved by this test stress.
planned.proof_route: Specify field units independently; with dimensionless psi, Q has inverse-length-squared components and is a mathematical energy tensor, not automatically SI matter stress.

planned.interface: For every smooth psi and X, nabla^a J_a^X=(box_g psi)X(psi)+(1/2)Q^ab (L_X g)_ab. Thus on-shell Killing currents are divergence free.
planned.proof_route: Differentiate Q, cancel Hessian terms using symmetry for scalars and metric compatibility, then symmetrize Q_ab nabla^a X^b.

planned.interface: For a smooth solution on a finite regular Schwarzschild exterior slab, the future stationary Killing current has nonnegative flux through spacelike slices and the future horizon, with balance including the outer boundary. The slice energy degenerates at the horizon where the Killing vector becomes null.
planned.proof_route: Use the dominant-energy inequality of Q in a Lorentz orthonormal frame and the divergence theorem on truncated regular domains; pass to the horizon only with smooth extendibility and integrable traces.

planned.interface: Let E:[0,Tmax)->[0,infinity) be continuous, with local existence, and suppose a solution extends past every finite T when sup_[0,T] E<=eta and all separately listed gauge/coercivity margins persist. A bootstrap estimate is an implication E<=2A epsilon^2 on [0,T] implies E<=A epsilon^2 on that interval, for constants A>0 and 2A epsilon^2<eta.
planned.proof_route: This is an abstract mathematical contract. Every application must identify E, norms, parameter modulation and the continuation criterion; the definition does not establish any Einstein estimate.

planned.interface: Under the contract, initial E(0)<A epsilon^2 and an improvement valid on every compact subinterval give E(t)<=A epsilon^2 on the whole maximal interval; if the listed margins persist, Tmax=infinity.
planned.proof_route: Use continuity to obtain the first bootstrap interval. The supremum time of the 2A bound cannot end before Tmax because the A improvement leaves a strict margin. If Tmax were finite, the continuation hypothesis contradicts maximality.

planned.interface: The accessed Klainerman-Szeftel 2021 manuscript describes a nonlinear asymptotically flat vacuum stability theorem for |a|/M sufficiently small and a multi-paper proof. Its abstract is evidence of the scoped result claimed by those authors, not a local proof, a certification of every companion, or a status survey of all subextremal Kerr as of 2026-10-19. No logical consumer uses this remark.
planned.proof_route: Read source title, abstract and scope; retain exact restriction and distinguish the announced theorem from the locally proved abstract bootstrap lemma.

planned.interface: On I times T^3 take g=-c^2 dt^2+sum_i a_i(t)^2(dx^i)^2 with positive C^2 lengths a_i and dimensionless periodic x^i. Define H_i=adot_i/a_i, H=(sum H_i)/3, V=a_1 a_2 a_3 and sigma^2=(1/2)sum_i(H_i-H)^2. Adopt the vacuum Einstein equation for the Kasner branch.
planned.proof_route: This is a spatially homogeneous ansatz; it does not cover arbitrary anisotropic or inhomogeneous cosmologies.

planned.interface: For t>0, a_i=A_i(t/t0)^p_i, A_i,t0>0, the diagonal Bianchi I metric is vacuum when sum p_i=sum p_i^2=1; the all-zero p_i case is separately flat. Conversely, a nonstatic power-law vacuum ansatz obeys these two equations.
planned.proof_route: Compute R_tt=-(sum_i(p_i^2-p_i))/t^2 and R_ii=(a_i^2/(c^2t^2))p_i(sum_j p_j-1). If any p_i differs from zero the second set forces sum p=1, and the first then gives sum p^2=1.

planned.interface: For a diagonal Bianchi I Einstein model with isotropic spatial stress, subtracting the spatial diagonal equations gives d(H_i-H_j)/dt+3H(H_i-H_j)=0. Thus V(H_i-H_j) is constant and sigma^2 is proportional to V^-2.
planned.proof_route: Subtract R_i^i-R_j^j; the trace and isotropic matter terms cancel. Since Vdot=3HV, multiply by V and integrate.

planned.interface: Input N>=3, grid spacing h=2pi/N, time step k>0, integer step count nmax>=1, periodic arrays u0 and v0. Define D_h u_j=(u_(j+1)-2u_j+u_(j-1))/h^2. Set u1=u0+k v0+(k^2/2)D_h u0; for n=1,...,nmax-1 output u_(n+1)=2u_n-u_(n-1)+k^2 D_h u_n with indices modulo N.
planned.proof_route: The procedure is finite and exact in real arithmetic; floating-point roundoff needs a separate model. It is a one-dimensional scalar hyperbolic benchmark, not an Einstein solver.

planned.interface: For admissible integer N,nmax the benchmark terminates after nmax-1 update loops, outputs all time levels through nmax, and uses O(N nmax) arithmetic operations.
planned.proof_route: Each loop has N explicit scalar updates, no nonlinear solve and a bounded counter.

planned.interface: For 0<k/h<1 each nonconstant Fourier mode has amplification roots on the unit circle with distinct roots except for the zero-frequency component; the latter represents the exact linear-in-time spatial mean and is controlled on fixed finite slabs. No uniform-in-time bound on displacement follows for nonzero mean velocity.
planned.proof_route: Diagonalize D_h with exp(2pi i l j/N). The root equation is z^2-2(1-2lambda^2 sin^2(pi l/N))z+1=0. For 0<lambda<1 and l!=0 its real middle coefficient has absolute value <2. Treat the repeated root z=1 for l=0 using the initial velocity.

planned.interface: For discrete metric/extrinsic-curvature data and a specified reconstruction/interpolation, define H_h and M_h by evaluating the signed Hamiltonian and momentum residuals with the chosen discrete derivative operators. Report the grid norm, units, mesh hierarchy, boundary treatment and reconstruction. A small residual is a diagnostic, not a proof of closeness to an exact development.
planned.proof_route: Define the actual discrete operators before every code experiment. Constraint convergence and solution convergence are separate claims.

planned.interface: Let L be a smooth local four-form Lagrangian for fields phi on an oriented four-manifold and let a chosen variational decomposition be delta L=E(phi) dot delta phi+d theta(phi;delta phi). For commuting smooth variations define omega(phi;delta1 phi,delta2 phi)=delta2 theta(phi;delta1 phi)-delta1 theta(phi;delta2 phi). For a compact oriented three-surface Sigma put Omega_Sigma=integral_Sigma omega.
planned.proof_route: Use Iyer-Wald ordering explicitly. Define variations as derivatives of a smooth two-parameter family, so commutation and passage through d/integrals have a stated regularity basis.

planned.interface: If E=0 and both variations obey delta_i E=0, then d omega=0. For a compact region with oriented boundary Sigma2-Sigma1+B, Omega_Sigma2-Omega_Sigma1=-integral_B omega.
planned.proof_route: Antisymmetrize the two variations of L: d omega=delta1 E dot delta2 phi-delta2 E dot delta1 phi under the chosen ordering. Apply finite-region Stokes. Cauchy independence requires zero boundary flux, not on-shell closure alone.

planned.interface: Replacing L by L+d mu and theta by theta+delta mu+dY changes omega by d(delta2 Y(delta1)-delta1 Y(delta2)); the delta mu terms cancel. Consequently Omega on a compact surface changes by the corresponding integral over its boundary.
planned.proof_route: Commute variations, use delta_i d=d delta_i and surface Stokes. A boundary condition may kill the corner term; covariance alone does not.

planned.interface: On a specified solution space with specified admissible variations and boundary conditions, call Omega presymplectic if it is closed but possibly degenerate. A reduced symplectic manifold exists only when the null distribution has a smooth quotient with a descended nondegenerate two-form. A Hamiltonian for an admissible vector field X satisfies i_X Omega=dH on that specified space.
planned.proof_route: Use the existing finite-dimensional reduction only for tangent linear models; it does not establish an infinite-dimensional smooth quotient. The library convention i_XH omega=dH fixes bracket signs.

planned.interface: On a trivializing patch let e^I be a smooth coframe, eta=diag(-1,1,1,1), g=eta_IJ e^I tensor e^J and omega^I_J an so(1,3)-valued one-form. Define torsion T^I=de^I+omega^I_J wedge e^J and curvature F^I_J=domega^I_J+omega^I_K wedge omega^K_J. Under eprime=Lambda e put omegaprime=Lambda omega Lambda^-1-dLambda Lambda^-1.
planned.proof_route: A local coframe need not extend globally. Distinguish a Lorentz connection from a spin lift; the title is an interface and not an assertion that a spin structure exists.

planned.interface: For a nondegenerate coframe there is exactly one eta-skew connection one-form with de^I+omega^I_J wedge e^J=0; its induced tangent connection is the metric-selected torsion-free connection. Under a Lorentz coframe change Fprime=Lambda F Lambda^-1 and Tprime=Lambda T.
planned.proof_route: Construct omega from the existing Levi-Civita connection in the frame. Conversely the Cartan torsion equation implies zero tangent torsion and eta-skewness gives metric compatibility; uniqueness follows from Levi-Civita. Expand the gauge law to cancel dLambda terms.

planned.interface: For an oriented time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, a Lorentzian spin structure is a principal Spin+(1,3) bundle with an equivariant double-cover map to the oriented time-oriented orthonormal SO+(1,3) frame bundle. The chosen spin representation gives its associated complex spinor bundle, and a lifted Lorentz connection differentiates spinors. This definition assumes a supplied smooth double cover and a chosen lift; it asserts neither lift existence nor uniqueness.
planned.proof_route: Define Spin+(1,3) concretely via SL(2,C) acting on Hermitian 2x2 matrices X=x0 I+x dot sigma by X->A X A dagger; det X=x0^2-|x|^2. Prove kernel {+I,-I}, local differential isomorphism and surjectivity onto the identity component before using the cover.

planned.interface: For gamma matrices with {gamma^I,gamma^J}=2eta^IJ I and omega_IJ=-omega_JI, the local spin covariant derivative D=d+(1/4)omega_IJ gamma^I gamma^J induces the vector Lorentz connection under Clifford multiplication. The assertion is local and presumes the selected spin representation.
planned.proof_route: Compute [gamma^I gamma^J,gamma^K]=2(eta^JK gamma^I-eta^IK gamma^J) and contract with omega_IJ. Fix raised/lowered gamma conventions before identifying the vector action.

planned.interface: For a C^1 path gamma:[0,1]->U and continuous matrix-valued omega(gammadot), define transport U_gamma as the endpoint solution Udot=-omega(gammadot)U, U(0)=I. Concatenation is piecewise C^1 with its orientation stated; reversal reverses the path.
planned.proof_route: Use linear ODE existence and uniqueness for finite-dimensional matrices. This defines tangent/associated-bundle transport, not foliation holonomy.

planned.interface: Transport obeys U_(gamma2*gamma1)=U_gamma2 U_gamma1, U_(gamma^-1)=U_gamma^-1, and under eprime=Lambda e, Uprime_gamma=Lambda(gamma(1)) U_gamma Lambda(gamma(0))^-1.
planned.proof_route: Solve separately on concatenated pieces and invoke uniqueness. Differentiate Lambda(gamma(t))U(t)Lambda(gamma(0))^-1 and substitute the connection transformation law. The resulting path groupoid functor need not factor through the fundamental groupoid unless curvature vanishes.

planned.interface: For a C^2 matrix connection on a coordinate rectangle based at p with side lengths epsilon in directions i then j, traversed in positive boundary order, U_loop=I-epsilon^2 F_ij(p)+O(epsilon^3) in a fixed local frame.
planned.proof_route: Expand the four segment ODE solutions through second order, including first derivatives of omega; multiplication yields -(partial_i omega_j-partial_j omega_i+[omega_i,omega_j])epsilon^2. Uniform C^2 bounds on a compact patch control the remainder.

planned.interface: For a finite oriented graph with compact group G=SU(2), assign g_e in G, g_reverse=g_e^-1; a vertex gauge transformation h_v acts by g_e->h_target g_e h_source^-1. A Wilson loop in a specified finite-dimensional unitary representation rho is tr rho(product of edge elements in path order). This is a finite configuration model, not an established continuum quantum theory of gravity.
planned.proof_route: Define the graph, path ordering, representation and group before taking trace. Vertex gauge invariance follows by endpoint cancellation and trace cyclicity. The SU(2) choice requires a separate time-gauge reduction for a gravity interpretation.

planned.interface: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a finite graph and prescribed finite-dimensional unitary edge representations of compact G=SU(2), form at each vertex the tensor product W_v of incoming representation spaces and outgoing dual representation spaces. The normalized Haar average P_v=integral_G R_v(g) dmu(g) is the orthogonal projection onto W_v^G. Products of these vertex projections impose the finite vertex gauge invariance condition on the graph coefficient tensor space; no Hamiltonian or continuum constraint is imposed.
planned.proof_route: Apply the exact Haar intertwiner projection with H=C carrying the trivial representation, J=W_v and T(1)=w. Its contraction/idempotence gives an invariant-vector projection. If P is a contractive idempotent on a Hilbert space, take x in its range and y in its kernel, and compare ||x||^2<=||x+t y||^2 for real and imaginary t to get orthogonality. Distinct vertex gauge actions commute on edge coefficient factors, so their projections commute.
